raw_response:
I'm 75 now, and I've been farming this same plot for 55 years. Never went to school — can't read those numbers on the fertilizer bags — but I know this land like I know my own hands. It's just me and my wife at home. Our children are in Shijiazhuang with their own families. We have 3 mu, wheat and maize, same as always.

For the wheat, I save my own seed every year and mix in a little new seed from the shop so it doesn't get weak. Costs almost nothing that way. Before planting in early October, right after the maize comes off, I put down about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu — what my father did, and what I've always done. In late March, if the wheat looks yellow at jointing, I topdress with some urea. I learned my lesson three years ago when I skipped the topdress to save money — spring turned dry and the yield was terrible. Wheat is our staple, we need the flour, so I irrigate three times. The pump costs electricity, but going hungry costs more.

For the maize, the window is tight — sometimes only a day between wheat harvest and planting in mid-June. I buy hybrid seed from the county store; can't save that, it won't grow right next year. All the fertilizer goes in at planting, half a bag per mu in the furrow. No time for split application, the season is too short. I irrigate twice if the rains don't come. Last summer was wet, but you can't count on that.

I don't hire labor — can't afford it, and on 3 mu we manage ourselves. Just slower now. My back hurts, my wife's knees hurt, but we get it done. I expect about 350-360 jin per mu of wheat and 400 of maize if the weather is decent. I'm not changing anything. At 75, new ideas are just new ways to lose money. I need enough grain for us to eat and a little to sell for medicine and cooking oil.
